note: Ps104 creation hymn (35v, 166 spans). Read by CHAR-ARC (not verse-blocks): the human IB lives in 3 arcs amid a vast creation-catalogue. ARC-A doxology frame: v1 'Bless the LORD O my soul... you are very great' <-> v35b 'Bless the LORD O my soul! Praise the LORD!' (bookends). ARC-B heart-provision v14-15: wine to GLADDEN the HEART, oil to make the face SHINE, bread to strengthen man's HEART. ARC-C closing response v33-35a: I will SING + SING-PRAISE, may my MEDITATION be PLEASING, I REJOICE in the LORD, let SINNERS/WICKED be consumed. Between (v2-13,16-32) = God's creative ACTS (qualifiers, source-linked to the doxology) + created THINGS (standalone) - substrate, not a char passage.

dims.v: paired with the soul, bookended at v35

v1: 'BLESS (barak) the LORD, O my soul! O LORD my God, you are very great!' - the self-summons that opens the hymn; the whole creation-catalogue that follows is the ground of this blessing. (Frame with v35.)
v1: 'Bless the LORD, O my SOUL (nephesh)!' - the innermost self roused to bless God for his works, the vantage from which the whole psalm is sung.
v35: 'BLESS (barak) the LORD, O my soul!' - the closing return of the frame; having surveyed all God's works, the soul comes back to bless. (Directly interrelated with v1, 269203.)
v35: 'Bless the LORD, O my SOUL (nephesh)!' - the innermost self, first and last called to bless the Creator.
v35: 'PRAISE (halal) the LORD!' - the first Hallelujah of the Psalter, sealing the creation-hymn with praise.
paired with the heart, and with the face that shines
v14-15: 'wine to GLADDEN (samach) the heart of man' - the inner lift God's provision gives, gladness as one of the ends of the harvest; the arc's centre.
paired with the gladdening, and with the strengthened heart (269249)
v15: 'wine to gladden the HEART (lebab) of man' - the inner seat God's gift reaches, the heart that wine cheers.
v15: 'oil to make his face SHINE (tsahal)' - the brightened countenance, the outward glow of the inner gladness God's provision brings.
v15: 'and bread to strengthen man's HEART (lebab)' - the heart sustained by food, the inner self upheld; parallel to the heart gladdened by wine.
to the LORD as long as he lives
v33: 'I will SING (shir) to the LORD as long as I live' - the lifelong vow of praise, the personal response to all God's works.
to God while he has being
v33: 'I will SING PRAISE (zamar) to my God while I have being' - the pledge of praise for as long as life lasts.
paired with rejoicing, and with its being pleasing
v34: 'May my MEDITATION (siach) be pleasing to him' - the inward musing on God the psalmist hopes God will accept, worship of the mind.
v34: 'may my meditation be PLEASING (arab) to him' - the acceptability sought for the inner worship, that the musing may delight God.
v34: 'for I REJOICE (samach) in the LORD' - the joy in God that fuels the song, gladness that is worship's spring.
v35: 'Let SINNERS (chatta) be consumed from the earth' - the one discordant note in the creation-praise, the wish that evil be cleared from God's good world.
v35: 'and let the WICKED (rasha) be no more!' - the wicked whose end the psalmist longs for, so creation's praise may be unmarred.
